history.dynasty: Kachhwaha (Amber/Jaipur) - built by Diwan Rao Kriparam, courtier of Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II
history.period: 18th century (verify - one weak source says 16th century, conflict flagged)
history.summary: Galtaji is an ancient pilgrimage site in a narrow Aravalli gorge about 10 km east of Jaipur, named after the sage Galav who performed tapasya here; legend says the gods blessed the spot with abundant water. The site has been a retreat for Ramanandi Vaishnav ascetics since the early 16th century; the present temple complex was built in the 18th century by Diwan Rao Kriparam, a courtier of Sawai Jai Singh II. The complex is built of pink sandstone with pavilions, rounded roofs, carved pillars and painted walls - resembling a Rajasthani haveli more than a conventional temple. Key elements: seven sacred kunds fed by a perennial spring emerging from a Gaumukh (cow-mouth) rock - the Galta Kund, holiest, is said never to run dry; the Surya Mandir (Sun Temple) on the highest peak, also built under Kriparam/Jai Singh II, with panoramic views of Jaipur (frescoes damaged by 1991 rains); the Balaji (Hanuman) shrine near the entrance; and the main Sita Ram (Ram Gopal Ji) temple - see CSV row 2074, which covers the same complex. The large rhesus macaque population makes it the 'Monkey Temple' (Galwar Bagh), featured in National Geographic's 'Rebel Monkeys'. Date conflict flagged: one source says the present temple dates to the 16th century; the majority say 18th century. name: Galtaji Temple (Surya Mandir / Balaji)
town: Jaipur (CSV town 'Galtaji (Jaipur)' normalized; actual locality Galta/Khania-Balaji, ~10 km east of Jaipur)
town_description: Galtaji lies in a narrow crevice of the Aravalli hills about 10 km east of Jaipur, past Surajpol and the Ghat ki Guni road, near Sisodia Rani ka Bagh on the Jaipur-Agra road. The gorge holds a natural spring, seven sacred kunds, and a series of pink-sandstone temples, and is home to a large, famous troop of rhesus macaques.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism - Ramanandi sect; Surya worship at the hilltop shrine)

travel.road: About 10 km east of Jaipur via the Ghat ki Guni/Surajpol road toward Agra; the climb from the entrance is about 2.5 km (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Makar Sankranti (mid-January) is the biggest festival day.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published in consulted sources (verify - confirm locally); the Surya Mandir climb takes about 20-30 minutes.
